How come that anime has horrible distribution and availability (when it comes to number of countries) compared to video games of Japanese origin?

Distribution is difficult because television is an aging medium, and online streaming is bogged down by licensing issues. Games have thriving online distribution platforms and are a truly global industry unlike anime, which is more niche.

Even still, I wouldn't say that availability of Japanese games in the West is stellar – take a look at some Japan-exclusive MMOs like PSO2 or Dragon's Dogma Online, which are actually pretty good games that many people from the West go to great lengths (VPN, unofficial translations) to play.

There's also the matter of the audience's mindset – many years of abysmal availability have caused anime viewers to become strongly accustomed to piracy, and even if someone's not a die-hard pirate they may refuse to sub to legal streams which are infested with Flash, DRM, region restrictions and other BS.
So a vicious cycle of financial loss?
